title: Stalk faithfulness for derived objects
statement:
A morphism in $D(T_{\Et})$ is an isomorphism if and only if its
pullback to every geometric point of $T$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ and a morphism $\alpha:K\to L$ in $D(T_{\Et})$. By [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] this is a triangulated derived category; choose a distinguished cone triangle $K\xrightarrow{\alpha}L\to C\to K[1]$ as in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Apply [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] to this triangle: $\alpha$ is an isomorphism if and only if $C$ is zero.

source.place: ## Proof, cone and cohomology-stalk argument, expanded

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar t:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] says that $\bar t^{-1}:\Ab(T_{\Et})\to\Ab(P_{\Et})$ is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], so termwise inverse image induces a functor on the unbounded derived categories which commutes with shift and preserves distinguished triangles. To see its action on the cone, use the explicit formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $C(f)^q=B^q\oplus A^{q+1}$ and $d_{C(f)}=\begin{pmatrix}d_B&f\\0&-d_A\end{pmatrix}$. Additivity and preservation of finite sums send this matrix, its inclusion and its negative projection to the same cone data for $\bar t^{-1}f$. Thus the image of the triangle of step 1 is the distinguished triangle $K_{\bar t}\xrightarrow{\alpha_{\bar t}}L_{\bar t}\to C_{\bar t}\to K_{\bar t}[1]$ in $D(P_{\Et})$. The termwise inverse image is the derived pullback (and, after identifying point sheaves with groups, the derived stalk) of [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback].

source.place: ## Proof, first and final cone sentences; Stacks Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, for termwise exact pullback, and the displayed cone calculation

proof.text: For every integer $q$ and geometric point $\bar t$, [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology] identifies $\mathcal H^q(C)_{\bar t}$ with $\mathcal H^q(C_{\bar t})$. The equality is understood using the equivalence $\Gamma(P,-):\Ab(P_{\Et})\simeq\Ab$ of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], not as a literal equality between a sheaf and a group. An equivalence preserves and reflects zero objects: the unique maps to and from a zero object transport under a fully faithful, essentially surjective functor. Consequently $\mathcal H^q(C)_{\bar t}=0$ if and only if the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q(C_{\bar t})$ on $P$ is zero.

source.place: ## Proof, cone and cohomology-stalk argument, expanded

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the morphism $0\to\mathcal H^q(C)$ of abelian etale sheaves. The stalk of the zero sheaf is zero because the stalk functor is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. Hence this morphism is an isomorphism exactly when all $\mathcal H^q(C)_{\bar t}$ vanish. This proves $\mathcal H^q(C)=0$ if and only if all its geometric stalks vanish; no conservativity statement for derived objects has been used here.

source.place: ## Proof, cone and cohomology-stalk argument, expanded

proof.text: By [lem-kun-d-zero-cohomology] on $T$, $C=0$ if and only if $\mathcal H^q(C)=0$ for every integer $q$. Step 4 makes this equivalent to vanishing of $\mathcal H^q(C)_{\bar t}$ for all $q,\bar t$. Step 3 makes it equivalent to vanishing of every cohomology sheaf of every $C_{\bar t}$. Interchange the two universal quantifiers and apply [lem-kun-d-zero-cohomology] on each scheme $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: the condition is exactly $C_{\bar t}=0$ for every geometric point. Finally [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] applied to each distinguished triangle of step 2 says that $C_{\bar t}=0$ if and only if $\alpha_{\bar t}$ is an isomorphism. Combining this with step 1 gives both implications of the statement, with no boundedness restriction.
